snapshot.title: Tiny text classifier
snapshot.summary: Original stdlib Naive Bayes exercise with four training and two synthetic test rows. No pretrained weights, real dataset, fairness study or general accuracy claim.

categoryEvidence.task: Classify tiny English snippets into synthetic positive or negative labels.
categoryEvidence.datasetModelLicense: Four training and two test strings and classifier code are original MIT material; no external model.
categoryEvidence.splits: TRAIN has four handwritten rows; TEST has two held-out handwritten rows in the same toy vocabulary.
categoryEvidence.evaluation: Fixed deterministic hold-out exercise; no cross-validation or population sampling.
categoryEvidence.metrics: 2 of 2 toy test rows classified correctly; 1.0 accuracy applies only to those two rows.
categoryEvidence.inference: classifier.py exposes classify(text); ignores unseen vocabulary and ties follow a deterministic label order.
categoryEvidence.limitations: Not suitable for real sentiment, languages beyond toy English, safety decisions or academic performance claims.
